title: Keep the analyzer working when source generation is suppressed

lines.text: > Note: When using Unity, dynamic code generation only works when targeting .NET Framework 4.x + mono runtime.
For all other Unity targets, AOT is required.
A `[MessagePackObject]` type can opt out of source generation with `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`.
No formatter is generated for that type. It is serialized at run time by the dynamic resolvers, which use reflection, so such a type is not AOT-safe.
The analyzer still validates these types, because they are serialized at run time and must still have a valid contract:
- Keys are unique and all of the same kind ([MsgPack005](doc/analyzers/MsgPack005.md)).
- Members have types that are themselves serializable ([MsgPack003](doc/analyzers/MsgPack003.md)).
- Types are accessible to the resolver ([MsgPack012](doc/analyzers/MsgPack012.md)).

The analyzer does not report the partial-class requirement ([MsgPack011](doc/analyzers/MsgPack011.md)) or the AOT-only checks ([MsgPack016](doc/analyzers/MsgPack016.md) and [MsgPack017](doc/analyzers/MsgPack017.md)) for these types, because they only apply when a formatter is generated.
You can customize the generated source through properties on the `GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute`.
continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.
continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.
throw new InsufficientExecutionStackException($"This msgpack sequence has an object graph that exceeds the maximum depth allowed of {MaximumObjectGraphDepth}.");

public string Prop1 { get; init; } = ""some default"";

requirement.title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement.intent: The analyzer must report its diagnostics for types that set SuppressSourceGeneration = true, as it did in version 3.1.0.

functional.text: The analyzer reports diagnostics for a [MessagePackObject] type with SuppressSourceGeneration = true.
The analyzer behaves for such types as it did in version 3.1.0, before the regression in 3.1.1.

nonFunctional.text: The analyzer must not crash on invalid input in a suppressed type; it reports the problem instead. (inferred)
Types that do not suppress source generation keep their current diagnostics. (inferred)

expectedBehaviours: Building a project with a [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] type that breaks an analyzer rule (for example a missing [Key] on a public member) shows the matching MsgPack diagnostic in the build output and the IDE.
Setting SuppressSourceGeneration = true no longer silences the analyzer: the type still gets analyzed even though no formatter is generated for it.
The source generator still writes no formatter for the suppressed type.
expectedTests: An analyzer test with a SuppressSourceGeneration = true type that is missing a Key attribute expects the matching MsgPack diagnostic at the member's location.
A generator snapshot test checks that a suppressed type still produces no formatter output while the diagnostics are reported.

expectedBehaviours: For suppressed types, the analyzer reports the same diagnostic IDs, severities and locations that version 3.1.0 reported for the same source.
Code that compiled cleanly with no diagnostics under 3.1.0 still compiles with no extra diagnostics for suppressed types.
expectedTests: A regression test reproduces the case from the issue and checks the diagnostics match the 3.1.0 results.
A test with a valid suppressed type checks that no diagnostics are reported.

expectedBehaviours: When a suppressed type has invalid input (for example duplicate keys, mixed key types, or a member type that cannot be resolved), the analyzer reports a diagnostic and does not throw.
The build log shows no AD0001 analyzer-exception warning and no generator crash warning for such types.
The rest of the compilation's diagnostics still get reported.
expectedTests: An analyzer test with a suppressed type that has duplicate or conflicting Key values expects the matching MsgPack diagnostic and no AD0001.
A test with a suppressed type whose member type is unresolvable checks that the analyzer finishes without an exception.

expectedBehaviours: Types without SuppressSourceGeneration, or with it set to false, show exactly the diagnostics they showed before the change.
Formatters and resolvers generated for non-suppressed types are unchanged, so the existing snapshot files under Resources still match.
No duplicate diagnostics show up for any type.
expectedTests: The existing analyzer and generator snapshot tests pass without any changes to their expected outputs.
A test with both a suppressed and a non-suppressed invalid type in one compilation checks that each diagnostic is reported exactly once.

story.what: In TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo, a member whose key kind (int or string) differs from the first keyed member is now skipped once the DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys diagnostic has been reported. Before each Add to intMembers or stringMembers, the code now checks for an existing key, so a duplicate key no longer throws inside the analyzer and only the first member with that key is kept. Both changes apply to properties and fields. The change also adds analyzer tests and execution tests for SuppressSourceGeneration types, a README section that lists which diagnostics still apply to them, and an edit to MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep that changes its comparison from >= to >.
story.why: Requirement MP-2234 says the analyzer stopped reporting diagnostics for [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] types. The analyzer has to validate these types again and must not crash on invalid input such as duplicate or mixed keys; it should report a diagnostic instead. The new tests target exactly those cases.

touches.note: Skips members with a mismatched key kind and guards the dictionary Add calls against duplicate keys, for both properties and fields.
The depth check now uses > instead of >= when compared with MaximumObjectGraphDepth.
New analyzer tests for suppressed types, plus one test for a non-suppressed type.
New execution tests: no generated formatter exists for a suppressed type, and the type round-trips through the dynamic resolver.

findings.title: Null key on first keyed field still crashes the analyzer
findings.detail: In the field loop, a field with [Key(null)] that is the first keyed member reports BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull. It then sets isIntKey = false (searchFirst path), skips the mismatch check, and reaches the else branch, which calls stringMembers.ContainsKey(stringKey!) with a null key. Dictionary.ContainsKey(null) throws ArgumentNullException, so the analyzer fails with AD0001 instead of only reporting the diagnostic. This happens for suppressed and non-suppressed types alike. N1 says the analyzer must not crash on invalid input in a suppressed type. The new guards in h7 do not cover this path, because a null key never reaches the ContainsKey check added there.

findings.title: Skipping mixed-key members drops nested diagnostics on their types
findings.detail: The new continue after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys exits before the recursive CollectCore(item.Type, item) call at the end of the iteration. When a member's key kind does not match, its type is no longer analyzed. Diagnostics on that type, such as MsgPack003 for a type that is not a MessagePackObject, stop being reported until the key is fixed. This applies to non-suppressed types too, so their diagnostics change, against N2. It also partly contradicts the README's promise that member types of suppressed types are checked.

findings.title: No test for unresolvable member type in suppressed type
findings.detail: N1 expects a test showing that the analyzer finishes without an exception when a suppressed type has a member whose type cannot be resolved. The new tests cover duplicate and mixed keys, but no test uses an error type, so the CollectCore path for such members is not exercised.

findings.title: No test of suppressed and normal invalid types together
findings.detail: N2 expects a test where a suppressed and a non-suppressed invalid type share one compilation, checking that each diagnostic is reported exactly once. The new tests put each type in its own compilation, so double reporting across types is not checked.

refusals.reason: The change loosens the nesting-depth limit that MessagePackSecurity.DepthStep applies to untrusted input, from >= to >, which allows one more level. It also leaves the doc comment saying 'at or exceeds'. The requirement does not ask for this, and it is a security-design decision for the security owner.
